title: A pendulum is a spring
summary: Build a mass on a spring that keeps time with a pendulum, then swing the pendulum wide enough to break the match.

steps.title: The pendulum's clock
steps.text:
A 1 m pendulum swinging 5°, without damping. For small swings, gravity pulls the bob back with a torque close to m g L θ: proportional to the angle, like a spring. That gives simple harmonic motion with period

    T = 2π √(L / g) = 2.006 s

Run it and read the measured period in the Summary.

check.hint: Load the setup and press Run.
check.success: 2.007 s, within 0.05 % of 2π√(L/g). Now build a spring that keeps the same time.

steps.title: A spring that keeps time
steps.text:
A mass on a spring oscillates at ωn = √(k/m), and the small-angle pendulum at ω = √(g/L). They match when

    k / m = g / L

This mass is 2 kg. Set the stiffness k so that the spring keeps time with the 1 m pendulum, and run. (Damping is off.)

check.success: k = 19.62 N/m gives ωn = 3.132 rad/s, a period 2π/ωn = 2.006 s, the pendulum's. Only the ratio k/m matters, just as the pendulum's mass drops out of g/L.

steps.title: Swing it harder
steps.text:
A spring's period doesn't depend on how far you stretch it: try x₀ = 1 m on the spring and ωn stays the same. Is the pendulum the same?

Back on the pendulum, release it from 90° and run. Compare the measured period with the small-angle period.

check.success: 2.37 s, 18 % slower than the spring. The Angle plot shows the small-angle model drifting ahead of the real swing.

steps.title: Where the match breaks
steps.text: Why does the wide swing take longer than the spring that matched it at 5°?

options: Gravity's torque grows as sin θ, slower than θ: at large angles the pull back is weaker than a spring's, so the swing slows
The bob has more energy, so it moves faster and the period gets shorter
Air resistance acts on the wide swing
check.success: At 90° the restoring torque is only 64 % of the linear spring's. The pendulum is a spring only for small angles; that is why a pendulum clock swings just a few degrees.
